en: Contrary to older textbooks stating 7,107, the Philippines actually has 7,641 islands.
Unlike most Philippine islands, Palawan is geologically part of the Asian continental shelf, not the oceanic crust.
Although it generally flows toward Manila Bay, the Pasig River actually reverses direction during high tide.
Contrary to its current fame, Mount Pinatubo was just a low, heavily forested mountain before 1991.
Despite its name, the Philippine eagle primarily hunts flying lemurs called colugos, not actual monkeys.
Although many mistakenly think Taal is the largest, Laguna de Bay actually holds that title.
Although common water buffaloes live nationwide, the rare tamaraw is found exclusively on the island of Mindoro.
Despite their volcanic cone shape, the Chocolate Hills are actually made of marine limestone, not volcanic rock.
Unlike countries with four distinct seasons, the Philippines only experiences the wet and dry seasons.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is not a single province, but rather an administrative area composed of six provinces.
Contrary to popular belief, Mount Apo is a dormant volcano, not an actively erupting one.
Despite its name, the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River actually emerges above ground before finally reaching the sea.
